theory.overview: Strings are sequences of characters that form the foundation of text processing in computing. Unlike arrays of numbers, strings have unique properties: they're immutable in many languages, have special encoding considerations (ASCII, UTF-8, UTF-16), and support a rich set of operations like searching, matching, and transformation. Understanding strings deeply is crucial for text processing, parsing, and many algorithmic problems. This chapter covers string representation in memory, common string operations, pattern matching algorithms, and classic string problems you'll encounter in interviews and real applications.

sections.title: String Representation in Memory
sections.content: Strings are stored as contiguous character arrays, typically with a null terminator ('\0') in C or with explicit length in higher-level languages. Each character uses 1 byte for ASCII or variable bytes for Unicode (UTF-8 uses 1-4 bytes, UTF-16 uses 2-4 bytes). String length is either stored separately (Python, Java) or determined by scanning for null terminator (C). The choice affects performance: length lookup is $O(1)$ with explicit length, $O(n)$ with null terminator. Concatenation can be expensive in immutable strings—each operation creates a new string and copies all characters, leading to $O(n^2)$ for repeated concatenation in a loop.
keyPoints: ASCII: 1 byte per character, 256 possible characters
UTF-8: Variable 1-4 bytes, backward compatible with ASCII
Null terminator: '\0' marks end in C-style strings
Immutable strings: operations create new copies

sections.title: String Operations Complexity
sections.content: Understanding the cost of string operations is critical. Access by index is $O(1)$—direct offset calculation. Searching for a substring is $O(n \times m)$ naive, but $O(n + m)$ with KMP or $O(nm)$ average with Rabin-Karp. Concatenation: $O(n + m)$ where $n$ and $m$ are lengths. Substring extraction: $O(k)$ where $k$ is substring length (copy required). String comparison: $O(k)$ where $k$ is length of shorter string (character by character). These operations form building blocks for more complex algorithms.

complexityTable.explanation: $O(1)$ with stored length, $O(n)$ scanning for null
Copy both strings to new buffer

sections.title: Pattern Matching Algorithms
sections.content: Finding a pattern string $P$ within text string $T$ is a fundamental problem. Naive approach slides $P$ through $T$, comparing at each position—$O(n \times m)$ time. Knuth-Morris-Pratt (KMP) uses a failure function to avoid rechecking known matches, achieving $O(n + m)$. Boyer-Moore skips characters by comparing from right to left and using bad-character and good-suffix heuristics—often sublinear in practice. Rabin-Karp uses rolling hash for $O(n + m)$ average, useful for multiple pattern search.

sections.title: String Manipulation Techniques
sections.content: Two-pointer technique is powerful for string problems. For reversing: swap characters from both ends moving inward ($O(n)$ time, $O(1)$ space). For removing duplicates in sorted string: two pointers—write pointer tracks unique characters, read pointer scans. For palindrome checking: two pointers from ends, compare while moving inward. Sliding window works for substring problems—maintain window and update incrementally. String builder pattern in mutable strings (StringBuilder in Java, list of chars in Python) avoids $O(n^2)$ concatenation cost.

sections.title: String Encoding and Unicode
sections.content: ASCII encodes 128 characters using 7 bits (1 byte). Extended ASCII adds 128 more. Unicode supports all characters with 1,114,112 code points. UTF-8 uses variable length: 1 byte for ASCII, 2-4 bytes for others. UTF-16 uses 2 bytes for BMP characters, 4 bytes for others. UTF-32 uses fixed 4 bytes. Encoding matters for string length (byte count vs character count) and indexing. In UTF-8, you can't safely index by byte offset—must parse characters. Most languages handle this transparently, but understanding it prevents bugs with international text.

keyConcepts.name: Immutability
keyConcepts.description: Strings in many languages cannot be modified in place. Operations create new strings. This affects performance—concatenation in loops is $O(n^2)$.
keyConcepts.solution: Use StringBuilder or mutable character arrays for repeated modifications

keyConcepts.name: Null Terminator
keyConcepts.description: C-style strings end with '\0'. Length determined by scanning until terminator. Cannot contain null byte in valid string.
keyConcepts.tradeoff: Length lookup $O(n)$, but saves storage for length field

keyConcepts.name: Character Encoding
keyConcepts.description: How characters map to bytes. ASCII (1 byte), UTF-8 (1-4 bytes), UTF-16 (2-4 bytes). Affects memory usage and byte-level operations.
keyConcepts.implication: String length ≠ byte count in variable-length encodings

keyConcepts.name: Rolling Hash
keyConcepts.description: Hash computed incrementally for sliding window. $H_{i+1} = (H_i - c_{i} \times d^{k-1}) \times d + c_{i+k}$. Enables $O(1)$ hash update when window slides.

steps.title: Initialize Pointers
steps.description: Set up pointers at appropriate positions (both ends for reversal, start for search, etc.)

steps.title: Compare Characters
steps.description: Compare characters at pointer positions based on operation (equality for palindrome, pattern matching)

steps.title: Process or Move
steps.description: Swap characters for reversal, move pointers for search, update hash for rolling hash

steps.title: Advance Pointers
steps.description: Move pointers inward or forward based on algorithm requirements

steps.title: Check Termination
steps.description: Check if pointers crossed or pattern found. Return result or continue.

practiceProblems.title: Valid Palindrome
practiceProblems.description: Given a string, determine if it's a palindrome, considering only alphanumeric characters and ignoring case.
practiceProblems.example: Input: 'A man, a plan, a canal: Panama'. Output: true
practiceProblems.solution: Two pointers from ends. Skip non-alphanumeric. Compare lowercase characters. Move inward. If all match, return true.

practiceProblems.title: Longest Palindromic Substring
practiceProblems.description: Find the longest palindromic substring in a string.
practiceProblems.solution: Expand around center. For each character (and between characters), expand outward while palindrome. Track maximum length. Or use Manacher's algorithm for $O(n)$.
hints: Consider odd and even length palindromes
For each position, expand both ways

practiceProblems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
practiceProblems.description: Find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
practiceProblems.solution: Sliding window with hash map. Track character → index. When duplicate found, move start to max(start, last_index + 1). Update max length.
hints: Hash map stores last seen index of each character
When duplicate, move window start past duplicate

practiceProblems.title: Valid Anagram
practiceProblems.description: Given two strings, check if they're anagrams (contain same characters with same frequency).
practiceProblems.solution: Count character frequencies in array of size 26. Increment for s, decrement for t. If any count non-zero, not anagram. Or sort both and compare.
hints: Sort and compare is $O(n \log n)$ alternative

practiceProblems.title: Group Anagrams
practiceProblems.description: Group anagrams together from an array of strings.
practiceProblems.solution: For each string, sort characters to get key. Use hash map: key → list of strings. Return all values. Or use character count as key.
hints: Use sorted string as hash map key
Character count array as key avoids sorting

practiceProblems.title: Longest Common Prefix
practiceProblems.description: Find the longest common prefix string amongst an array of strings.
practiceProblems.solution: Take first string as reference. Compare each character with all other strings. Stop when mismatch found. Return prefix up to that point.
hints: Compare character by character across all strings

practiceProblems.title: String to Integer (atoi)
practiceProblems.description: Convert string to 32-bit signed integer, handling whitespace, signs, overflow, and invalid input.
practiceProblems.solution: Skip whitespace. Check for sign. Build number digit by digit. Check for overflow before each addition. Stop at non-digit. Clamp to INT_MIN/INT_MAX.
hints: Build number digit by digit: result = result * 10 + digit

practiceProblems.title: Integer to String (itoa)
practiceProblems.description: Convert integer to string representation, handling negative numbers and zero.
practiceProblems.solution: Handle zero and negative. Extract digits by modulo 10, reverse order. Use character array, fill from end. Add sign if negative. Reverse or fill correctly.
hints: Extract digits: num % 10 gives last digit
Digits come out in reverse order
Fill string from end or reverse at end

practiceProblems.title: Implement strStr()
practiceProblems.description: Return index of first occurrence of needle in haystack, or -1 if not found.
practiceProblems.solution: Slide needle through haystack. At each position, compare characters. If all match, return index. If end reached, return -1. Can optimize with KMP.
hints: Compare character by character at each position

practiceProblems.title: Count and Say
practiceProblems.description: Generate nth term of count-and-say sequence: 1, 11, 21, 1211, 111221, ... (read previous term)
practiceProblems.solution: Iterative: start with '1'. For each step, read current term: count consecutive same digits, append count then digit. Repeat n-1 times.
hints: Build new string from counts and digits

practiceProblems.title: Minimum Window Substring
practiceProblems.description: Find minimum window in s containing all characters of t (including duplicates).
practiceProblems.solution: Sliding window with two pointers. Count characters in t. Expand right pointer, include characters. When all required found, contract left pointer to minimize window. Track minimum.
hints: Sliding window: expand right, contract left
Track required vs current character counts
When all found, try to shrink window

practiceProblems.title: Check Inclusion
practiceProblems.description: Check if s2 contains permutation of s1.
practiceProblems.solution: Sliding window of size len(s1). Count characters in s1. Slide window through s2, update counts. When counts match, return true.

practiceProblems.title: Reorganize String
practiceProblems.description: Rearrange string so no two adjacent characters are same. Return empty if impossible.
practiceProblems.solution: Count character frequencies. Use max heap: always pick most frequent character not same as previous. Place, decrement count, push back. If any character count > (n+1)/2, impossible.
hints: Most frequent character must be placed first
Use max heap to always pick most frequent

practiceProblems.title: Basic Calculator
practiceProblems.description: Evaluate expression string with +, -, (, ).
practiceProblems.solution: Use stack for signs. When seeing number, add with current sign. When seeing '(', push result and sign, reset. When seeing ')', pop and combine.

practiceProblems.title: Decode Ways
practiceProblems.description: Given encoded message where 'A'=1, 'B'=2, ..., 'Z'=26, count ways to decode.
practiceProblems.solution: DP: dp[i] = ways to decode up to i. dp[i] = dp[i-1] if s[i-1] valid, + dp[i-2] if s[i-2:i] valid (10-26). Space-optimized to two variables.
hints: DP: ways to decode depends on previous 1-2 characters
Single digit (1-9) and two digits (10-26) both valid
Space-optimized: only need previous two values

practiceProblems.title: Word Break
practiceProblems.description: Given string and word dictionary, determine if string can be segmented into space-separated dictionary words.
practiceProblems.solution: DP: dp[i] = true if s[0:i] can be segmented. For each i, check all words: if word matches ending at i and dp[i-len(word)] true, dp[i] = true.
hints: DP: can segment up to position i if any valid word ends at i
Check all dictionary words at each position

practiceProblems.title: Word Ladder
practiceProblems.description: Find shortest transformation sequence from beginWord to endWord, changing one letter at a time, using dictionary words.
practiceProblems.solution: BFS from beginWord. For each word, try changing each position to each letter. If in dict and not visited, add to queue. Track distance. Return when reach endWord.
hints: Use visited set to avoid cycles

practiceProblems.title: Reverse Words in String
practiceProblems.description: Reverse order of words in string, removing extra spaces.
practiceProblems.example: s='the sky is blue'. Output: 'blue is sky the'
practiceProblems.solution: Split by whitespace, reverse array, join with single space. Or two-pass: reverse entire string, then reverse each word individually.
hints: Split into words, reverse array, join
Or reverse entire string, then reverse each word

practiceProblems.title: Zigzag Conversion
practiceProblems.description: Write string in zigzag pattern on given rows, then read row by row.
practiceProblems.solution: Create row strings. Iterate through s, append to appropriate row based on direction (down/up). Change direction at top/bottom. Concatenate all rows.
hints: Change direction at row 0 and row numRows-1

practiceProblems.title: Find All Anagrams in String
practiceProblems.description: Find all start indices of p's anagrams in s.
practiceProblems.solution: Sliding window of size len(p). Count characters in p. Slide window through s, update counts. When counts match, add start index to result.

practiceProblems.title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
practiceProblems.description: Find length of longest substring with same letters after at most k replacements.
practiceProblems.solution: Sliding window. Track max frequency of any character in window. Window valid if (length - maxFreq) ≤ k. Expand right, shrink left if invalid. Track max length.
hints: Window valid if: length - max frequency ≤ k
Track max frequency in current window

practiceProblems.title: Multiply Strings
practiceProblems.description: Multiply two non-negative integers represented as strings, return product as string.
practiceProblems.solution: Simulate grade-school multiplication. Result array size n+m. For each digit in num1, multiply with each digit in num2, add to appropriate position. Handle carries.
hints: Result has at most n+m digits

practiceProblems.title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
practiceProblems.description: Serialize binary tree to string, deserialize string back to tree.
practiceProblems.solution: Serialize: BFS or DFS, use 'null' for missing. Join with delimiter. Deserialize: split string, reconstruct tree using same traversal.
hints: Use delimiter and marker for null

practiceProblems.title: Edit Distance
practiceProblems.description: Find minimum operations to convert word1 to word2 (insert, delete, replace).
practiceProblems.solution: DP: dp[i][j] = min operations to convert word1[0:i] to word2[0:j]. dp[i][j] = min(dp[i-1][j]+1, dp[i][j-1]+1, dp[i-1][j-1]+(word1[i-1]!=word2[j-1]))
hints: Base case: converting to/from empty string

practiceProblems.title: Distinct Subsequences
practiceProblems.description: Count number of distinct subsequences of s equal to t.
practiceProblems.solution: DP: dp[i][j] = distinct subsequences of s[0:i] equal to t[0:j]. If s[i-1]==t[j-1]: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + dp[i-1][j-1]. Else: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j].
hints: DP: count ways to match t in s
If characters match, can include or exclude s[i-1]

snippets.code:
# Bad: O(n²) due to repeated copying
s = ''
for i in range(1000):
    s += str(i)  # Creates new string each time

# Good: O(n)
parts = []
for i in range(1000):
    parts.append(str(i))
s = ''.join(parts)  # Single copy
